scope: Offline comparison of hard versus training-scaled logistic fitting targets from the same frozen joint-trained residual classifier. No new training, model selection, crop changes, observation weights or validation-mask changes. All 32 existing development photos remain, including six unresolved crops.
question: Does preserving the native continuous classifier score improve finished templates compared with fitting only its hard mask?
controls: Replay all 26 previous hard masks and all 26 confidence-arm hard masks exactly. Require identical scores/model/crop semantics, raw RGB, binary masks, observation coverage, geometry/paper/fidelity limits and ten-second solver allowances. The only candidate difference is sourceImage.probability = sigmoid(4 * raw native score), using the existing training loss temperature. Tiny Float32 half-threshold ties are disclosed; the validation mask is never changed.
evaluation: Run both methods freshly on every photo, rotating order. Independently render all exports and measure the same binary-mask/feature objective. Audit all editable exports and inspect every mask/weave panel. Compare final solver routing and errors; do not select a temperature or a checkpoint after inspecting results. Probabilities are training-scaled scores, not established real-photo calibration.
limitations: All real photos are repeatedly inspected development examples, not an untouched holdout.
The frozen classifier still confuses some printed ink and paper; soft fitting does not establish a corrected material mask.
Two fixed crops are visibly inappropriate, and six photos have no fixed crop; retain all of them.
A lower fitting objective does not replace binary-mask, feature, geometry or paper checks.
